title: Scheduler healing: lane restart, lease stabilization, and KV-cache shard granularity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce incidents and tail latency caused by long-lived scheduler lane stalls and coarse-grained KV-cache eviction. Implement a scheduler "healing" flow that can detect and safely restart stuck batch lanes, add shard-granular KV snapshotting to minimize eviction blast radius, and perform companion dependency upgrades necessary for safe concurrency and allocator behavior.
background: Over the past 9 months we've seen ~12 P99 latency incidents traced to scheduler lanes stuck on rare allocation patterns or unfair wake-ups during high-concurrency bursts. Current mitigation (full node drain + restart) is heavy and causes request loss and cascading cold KV-cache churn. Earlier refactors improved batching throughput but introduced a single global KV snapshot/eviction lock that amplifies restarts. This ticket consolidates previous fixes into an automated, testable healing path and modernizes a few low-level deps to reduce allocator and task-scheduler pathologies.
proposal: 1) Add per-lane health tracking and an idempotent lane-restart operation that quiesces in-flight sessions, snapshots local KV shards, and promotes warm caches into a short-lived staging region. 2) Replace global KV snapshot/evict with shard-level snapshotting and an atomic pointer-swap hot-swap for shard maps so restarts only rebuild the hot shards. 3) Upgrade async runtime and memory allocator (tokio 1.14 -> 1.16, bump futures/parking_lot where needed, swap jemalloc -> mimalloc on Linux builds) to reduce pause and scheduling anomalies. 4) Provide observability (lane restart events, shard-snapshot duration, staged-warm-hit-rate) and a canary for rollout with automatic rollback on quality regressions.
tasks: Design lane health state machine and failure modes (Aisha, Marco)
Implement per-lane health monitor and safe restart path (engine code)
Implement shard-level KV snapshot/restore and atomic shard map swap
Write integration tests that simulate stuck lanes, eviction storms, and partial shard failures
Benchmark before/after for p50/p95/p99 and throughput with synthetic burst workloads
Upgrade tokio and friends, run full test matrix and address any API breakages
Switch allocator on Linux builds to mimalloc and validate telemetry and memory scrubbing
Add telemetry: lane_restart.count, lane_restart.latency_ms, shard_snapshot.duration_ms, shard_warm_hit_rate
Create rollout plan and canary gating in Console; prepare rollback playbook
Document changes in runbook and mention in release notes
acceptance_criteria: Lane health monitor triggers restart for stuck lanes in unit and integration tests without request loss beyond configured tolerances
Shard-level snapshot reduces full-cache rebuild events in stress tests by >= 70% compared to baseline
No regressions in p50/p95 latency and p99 improves by at least 10ms on average in benchmark suite
Dependency upgrade completes with CI green across Linux/macOS (tokio/futures/parking_lot) and allocator switch passes leak/determinism checks
Telemetry surfaces restart events and warm-hit rates in Console; a canary rollout shows no SLO violations before promoting to 100%
Runbook includes clear rollback steps, and one postmortem drill executed in staging
dependencies: INF-1234 (build-toolchain-upgrade) - CI images must have mimalloc available
risks: Allocator change could expose subtle non-determinism in fuzz tests; mitigation: run extended CI with sanitizer builds
Async runtime upgrade may require touching many call sites; mitigation: staged compile-only branch and small API adapters
If shard-swap implementation is buggy, we could transiently serve stale KV entries; mitigation: conservative versioning and validation checksums on swap
Incorrect lane restart logic can cause request duplication; mitigation: idempotency markers and end-to-end test harness
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Canary at 5% traffic in a dedicated region for 48h with SLO/telemetry gating. 3) Expand to 25% for 24h. 4) If no regressions, expand to 100% and flip default. 5) If any gating metric trips, flip flag off and run rollback playbook.
